_about: The city objects palette (docs/design/city-objects-plan.md 3.2). Step 1 (solid classes) starts it with the classes alone: one row per class of collider face, the answer the car gets (H hard, S smash, P push, R ride, G ghost) and a note. Every class answers H in step 1, which is today's behaviour. Step 4 adds planned: the answer the research gives the class (docs/design/drivable-city.md 3: fences and hedges smash, parked cars are pushed, platforms are ridden over; walls by height and ground guard rails by what is behind them, here their hard default), shown by the collider view (--colliders, game/scripts/collider_view.gd); nothing else reads it. Step 2 adds the barrier types (types, see _types). game/scripts/solidity.gd reads it; map_builder.gd _solid and the dressing scripts' bodies name these ids (game/tools/check_solids.gd).

_types: Step 2 (the wall builder): one row per barrier type, today's looks, read by game/scripts/solidity.gd (types, type_row) and drawn by game/scripts/city_barriers.gd. id; family (heavy, light, low; nothing reads it yet: the later steps' panels and breaking); draw (slab: a box along the line, _wall_along; railing: posts and two rails you see through, _railing_along, on an upstand of `upstand` m in `colour`, posts and rails in `rail`, a post every `posts` m, every `posts_mapped` m on a line OpenStreetMap maps the fence type or a ball-stop net of; city_wall, guard_rail: their own builders); colour (hex, the body); thickness and height (m; height is the default when the line has no mapped `h`); h_range: a mapped height clamped to it; low_height, low_thickness: a mapped wall that low is that thin; material: the OSM `m` (tools/barrier_tags.py) whose colour, and unmapped height, the row gives a wall; placed: a street pass (game/data/road_objects.json), the bake's `st` (tools/object_fixes.py) or city_barriers.gd SITE_WALLS may name it, and an OSM line kind named so is drawn with it; note.
